items.summary: Financial AI systems must support decision-bearing questions involving payments, collections, cash flow, and compliance while ensuring numerical accuracy, traceability, and auditability. Large language models (LLMs) enable natural language interaction but cannot independently guarantee reproducible calculations or evidence-grounded recommendations. We present a production-grounded architecture integrating three components: a financial knowledge graph for enterprise relationships, temporal context, and provenance; a deterministic optimization engine for financial calculations and decisions; and a multi-agent LLM layer for intent interpretation, task orchestration, explanation, and claim validation. A coordination layer, termed context engineering, selects, ranks, composes, and validates query-specific context across ERP systems, tools, and tenants. Based on observations from 15 deployments over approximately 11 months, single-agent pipelines exhibited hallucination rates of about 7-9% (5-10% across query types), including invented invoices and unsupported financial claims. Graph-backed multi-agent validation reduced observed rates to below 1%, although these findings are observational rather than causal. ERP data quality and tenant-specific schemas remained major implementation challenges. Reusable mappings, graph templates, and validation policies coincided with a reduction in deployment time from roughly six to two weeks. We argue that financial context engineering extends beyond text-centric retrieval-augmented generation by requiring structured relationships, temporal validity, exact numerical evidence, access controls, and validation against source records and solver outputs. We outline research challenges in evaluation, reproducibility, privacy, context quality, and cross-tenant generalization.
items.title: Beyond LLM Wrappers: Context Engineering and the Three-Engine Architecture for Reliable Financial AI

items.summary: Supporting data and analysis code for the manuscript "Lifestyle-resolved fecal viromes reveal host-associated viral reservoirs and auxiliary metabolic divergence across animal feces". The retained dataset contains 166 fecal metagenomes (110 newly generated and 56 public), 15,106 representative vOTUs and 112 candidate auxiliary gene ORF-KO records across 105 vOTUs. The five archives provide processed data and figure sources; viral and candidate auxiliary gene sequences; the original 3,845-MAG local reference collection; assemblies for all 166 retained samples; and MAG annotation/host-comparison evidence. Raw reads are available under NCBI SRA BioProject PRJNA1454088 and the individual SRR/ERR accessions listed in the sample metadata. Version 1.1.0 is a documentation and Figure 1 reproducibility correction. It removes an unused constant input-target plotting-metadata column, provides observed QC yield fields, supplies Figure 1's required local source files, and documents the actual Holm/BH comparison families, Python-versus-R community-statistics implementations and KOfamScan-versus-DIAMOND evidence roles. Scientific sample membership, sequence payloads, abundance matrices, recorded KO calls and statistical result values are retained. The local MAG collection preserves original reference inputs, including two MAGs attributed to an excluded source sample; it is distinct from the 166-sample analysis subset. The deposit is not a newly validated one-command raw-read-to-figure workflow. Missing upstream processing/software provenance remains disclosed. The archived corrections do not certify that the separately submitted manuscript has already been synchronized. See README.txt and METHODS_AND_VERSION_CORRECTIONS.txt for precise scope and evidence.

items.summary: This record contains the source code, trained models, and derived research artifacts associated with the study “Physical fidelity and forecasting in compressed active matter representations.” The study evaluates how dimensionality reduction affects spatial reconstruction, physical fidelity, and temporal forecasting in active-matter simulations. It compares unconstrained, physics-constrained, realizability-constrained, and combined autoencoders with proper orthogonal decomposition (POD), at latent dimensions of 128, 256, and 512. Forecasting comparisons include linear autoregression, multilayer perceptrons, and persistence baselines. Reconstruction accuracy, physical admissibility, and forecast performance are treated as distinct evaluation objectives. The archive includes: • Source code for data acquisition, representation training, posthoc analysis, frozen final evaluation, and publication rendering. • Scientific configurations and dependency specifications. • Selected trained checkpoints, POD models, fitted forecasters, latent caches, training histories, and validation analyses. • Frozen final-test outputs, comparison summaries, coverage diagnostics, and provenance records. • Numerical visual exports, software tests, and workflow documentation. The original simulation data were downloaded from The Well, specifically its active_matter dataset. We acknowledge the original simulation contributors and the developers and curators of The Well. The original HDF5 simulation files are not redistributed in this record; the repository documents their acquisition, pinned revision, and content-hash verification. The Well: https://polymathic-ai.org/the_well/ Associated publication: https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.00568 Dataset documentation: https://polymathic-ai.org/the_well/datasets/active_matter/ Last-epoch checkpoints named last.pt are excluded; selected best.pt checkpoints are retained. Publication figures, tables, numerical source data, and supplementary videos are supplied with the manuscript submission and are excluded from this archive. Their public availability follows the release of the article and its supplementary materials. The code for generating those outputs remains included. The deposited ZIP contains 1,534 files and occupies approximately 26.18 GB. The accompanying README provides the archive’s SHA-256 checksum, a contents guide, installation references, and verification limits. Packaging integrity and source-checksum checks do not constitute an independent full-data replication. Some archived provenance records retain original execution paths; independent reruns should use a separate work directory and preserve the frozen results. Development repository: https://github.com/BioDecodingLab/Physically_Constrained_Representations_of_Active_Matter

items.summary: Learned surrogates of process simulators are often evaluated on random states from plants they have already seen. This technical report compares interpolation, leave-one-case-out, and leave-one-ore-group-out evaluation for five models trained on a steady-state mineral-processing simulator. The simulator tracks mineral mass over 63 size classes, water, closed grinding circuits, and unit-level balance closure. It reports limitations against published examples alongside the comparisons. On a 3,072-state design over twelve authored cases, the multilayer perceptron gives the lowest interpolation recovery RMSE (3.38 percentage points), but has a 26.24-point mean RMSE when each case is held out. The Gaussian process has the lowest mean held-out-case RMSE (10.95 points), while the perceptron has the highest median case-fold R-squared (0.547). Under ore-group holdout, the perceptron's median recovery R-squared is 0.437 across seven groups, but varies from 0.795 for the five chalcopyrite cases to -10.2 for the two gold-in-pyrite cases. Log-upgrade transfer is poor for every model. The cases are authored; these results do not establish performance on operating plants. The report documents the mineral-processing simulator, its physical models, machine-learning evaluation methods, a process-specific optimization study, data and preprocessing, validation protocols, limitations, and reproducibility. items.summary: Financial AI systems must support decision-bearing questions involving payments, collections, cash flow, and compliance while ensuring numerical accuracy, traceability, and auditability. Large language models (LLMs) enable natural language interaction but cannot independently guarantee reproducible calculations or evidence-grounded recommendations. We present a production-grounded architecture integrating three components: a financial knowledge graph for enterprise relationships, temporal context, and provenance; a deterministic optimization engine for financial calculations and decisions; and a multi-agent LLM layer for intent interpretation, task orchestration, explanation, and claim validation. A coordination layer, termed context engineering, selects, ranks, composes, and validates query-specific context across ERP systems, tools, and tenants. Based on observations from 15 deployments over approximately 11 months, single-agent pipelines exhibited hallucination rates of about 7-9% (5-10% across query types), including invented invoices and unsupported financial claims. Graph-backed multi-agent validation reduced observed rates to below 1%, although these findings are observational rather than causal. ERP data quality and tenant-specific schemas remained major implementation challenges. Reusable mappings, graph templates, and validation policies coincided with a reduction in deployment time from roughly six to two weeks. We argue that financial context engineering extends beyond text-centric retrieval-augmented generation by requiring structured relationships, temporal validity, exact numerical evidence, access controls, and validation against source records and solver outputs. We outline research challenges in evaluation, reproducibility, privacy, context quality, and cross-tenant generalization.

To test the pipeline, clone (make a copy of) the workspace following the instructions in this Terra Support guide . 3. items.summary: Supporting data and analysis code for the manuscript "Lifestyle-resolved fecal viromes reveal host-associated viral reservoirs and auxiliary metabolic divergence across animal feces". The retained dataset contains 166 fecal metagenomes (110 newly generated and 56 public), 15,106 representative vOTUs and 112 candidate auxiliary gene ORF-KO records across 105 vOTUs. The five archives provide processed data and figure sources; viral and candidate auxiliary gene sequences; the original 3,845-MAG local reference collection; assemblies for all 166 retained samples; and MAG annotation/host-comparison evidence. Raw reads are available under NCBI SRA BioProject PRJNA1454088 and the individual SRR/ERR accessions listed in the sample metadata. Version 1.1.0 is a documentation and Figure 1 reproducibility correction. It removes an unused constant input-target plotting-metadata column, provides observed QC yield fields, supplies Figure 1's required local source files, and documents the actual Holm/BH comparison families, Python-versus-R community-statistics implementations and KOfamScan-versus-DIAMOND evidence roles. Scientific sample membership, sequence payloads, abundance matrices, recorded KO calls and statistical result values are retained. The local MAG collection preserves original reference inputs, including two MAGs attributed to an excluded source sample; it is distinct from the 166-sample analysis subset. The deposit is not a newly validated one-command raw-read-to-figure workflow. Missing upstream processing/software provenance remains disclosed. The archived corrections do not certify that the separately submitted manuscript has already been synchronized. See README.txt and METHODS_AND_VERSION_CORRECTIONS.txt for precise scope and evidence.

items.summary: Financial AI systems must support decision-bearing questions involving payments, collections, cash flow, and compliance while ensuring numerical accuracy, traceability, and auditability. Large language models (LLMs) enable natural language interaction but cannot independently guarantee reproducible calculations or evidence-grounded recommendations. We present a production-grounded architecture integrating three components: a financial knowledge graph for enterprise relationships, temporal context, and provenance; a deterministic optimization engine for financial calculations and decisions; and a multi-agent LLM layer for intent interpretation, task orchestration, explanation, and claim validation. A coordination layer, termed context engineering, selects, ranks, composes, and validates query-specific context across ERP systems, tools, and tenants. Based on observations from 15 deployments over approximately 11 months, single-agent pipelines exhibited hallucination rates of about 7-9% (5-10% across query types), including invented invoices and unsupported financial claims. Graph-backed multi-agent validation reduced observed rates to below 1%, although these findings are observational rather than causal. ERP data quality and tenant-specific schemas remained major implementation challenges. Reusable mappings, graph templates, and validation policies coincided with a reduction in deployment time from roughly six to two weeks. We argue that financial context engineering extends beyond text-centric retrieval-augmented generation by requiring structured relationships, temporal validity, exact numerical evidence, access controls, and validation against source records and solver outputs. We outline research challenges in evaluation, reproducibility, privacy, context quality, and cross-tenant generalization.
items.title: Beyond LLM Wrappers: Context Engineering and the Three-Engine Architecture for Reliable Financial AI

items.summary: Online sensor telemetry feeds the digital-twin, forecasting, control, and maintenance tools of instrumented water infrastructure. Probes deployed in these assets silently accumulate drift, flatlines, volatility bursts, and outages that existing pipelines often miss, because detectors and imputers are evaluated separately and under inflated synthetic metrics, and decay is treated as isolated events. This work proposes HARDIO, a Health-Aware Reliable Detection-Imputation Orchestrator, an operational data-quality framework that pairs a duration-weighted sensor decay scorecard with a per-variable, chained detector-imputer benchmark. The assignment is selected by a four-pillar composite score (operational 35%, health coverage 30%, reconstruction 20%, calibration 15%) that scores the signal an operator actually receives after detection and imputation. HARDIO processes sensor installations independently, enabling parallel execution and avoiding the need to evaluate all plant channels jointly. HARDIO is validated on the Cheles wastewater treatment plant (WWTP), a real 1,177 population-equivalent (PE) plant, over 432 days, 19 channels, and eight sensor installations. No single detector-imputer pair is best for every channel, so detection and chained imputation distribute across SAITS, KNN Residual, and LSTM-AE. Chained quality is reported for all 19 channels using 1-NRMSE; relative R² is interpreted on the 16 channels where the signal variance makes it meaningful, and 12 of these exceed R²=0.90. On the held-out final 20% of the record (12 channels in five installations), HARDIO achieves a mean chained 1-NRMSE of 0.976, within 0.0035 of a per-channel oracle, and outperforms the uniform SAITS pipeline (p=0.003). Its reconstruction performance is close to that of the strongest uniform pipelines, without a statistically significant improvement over them, and slightly below that of a single detector-imputer pair selected on validation data (0.978). The released artefact exposes the model map, confidence labels, margins, and production masks for decision support.

items.summary: Supporting data and analysis code for the manuscript "Lifestyle-resolved fecal viromes reveal host-associated viral reservoirs and auxiliary metabolic divergence across animal feces". The retained dataset contains 166 fecal metagenomes (110 newly generated and 56 public), 15,106 representative vOTUs and 112 candidate auxiliary gene ORF-KO records across 105 vOTUs. The five archives provide processed data and figure sources; viral and candidate auxiliary gene sequences; the original 3,845-MAG local reference collection; assemblies for all 166 retained samples; and MAG annotation/host-comparison evidence. Raw reads are available under NCBI SRA BioProject PRJNA1454088 and the individual SRR/ERR accessions listed in the sample metadata. Version 1.1.0 is a documentation and Figure 1 reproducibility correction. It removes an unused constant input-target plotting-metadata column, provides observed QC yield fields, supplies Figure 1's required local source files, and documents the actual Holm/BH comparison families, Python-versus-R community-statistics implementations and KOfamScan-versus-DIAMOND evidence roles. Scientific sample membership, sequence payloads, abundance matrices, recorded KO calls and statistical result values are retained. The local MAG collection preserves original reference inputs, including two MAGs attributed to an excluded source sample; it is distinct from the 166-sample analysis subset. The deposit is not a newly validated one-command raw-read-to-figure workflow. Missing upstream processing/software provenance remains disclosed. The archived corrections do not certify that the separately submitted manuscript has already been synchronized. See README.txt and METHODS_AND_VERSION_CORRECTIONS.txt for precise scope and evidence.
items.title: Data and analysis code for Lifestyle-resolved fecal viromes reveal host-associated viral reservoirs and auxiliary metabolic divergence across animal feces

items.summary: Reproducibility package for the study "Feasibility-First Routing for Regulated Multi-Provider LLM Serving: Governance, Caching, and the Limits of Online Learning." It contains the governance-gate and routing/analysis code, the measured multi-provider inference records, figures, hypothesis documentation, an auditable decision-log sample, and the manuscript PDF. The study measures a governance gate that holds simulated-policy residency/BAA violations at 0% versus 38.5% for  governance-blind routing, an exact-match policy-scoped cache as the dominant cost lever, and an honest accuracy-cost trade-off for online (LinUCB) routing (-3.45 percentage points accuracy across 40 repeated benchmark re-splits while usually lowering modeled cost). All results reproduce from the saved records with numpy only; no new API calls are required. The code is licensed MIT; the package, text, figures, and data are licensed CC BY 4.0.

items.summary: This dataset contains the supplementary material to the article “Adaptive Event Disambiguation via Alignments with Deferred Decisions” , submitted to the journal Process Science. datasets/ : the two synthetically generated datasets used in the evaluation, each in its own folder ( blood_donation , smart_home ). Each folder contains: runs.txt : the normative process behavior as a set of reference runs (one run per line), i.e. the model log against which traces are aligned. Activities are encoded as single symbols. labels.json : the mapping between activity labels and the symbols used in runs.txt . ambiguous.xes : the ambiguous event log, i.e. a set of traces in which events affected by ambiguity carry all their competing candidate activity labels. gold_standard.xes : the corresponding unambiguous log, used as ground truth for measuring disambiguation accuracy. Each log describes 15,000 executions of a process: Blood donation (BD): a blood-donation process synthesized from 32 real executions in an IoT-augmented lab setup. Smart home (SH): a smart-home process derived from the BP-Meets-IoT 2020 challenge dataset ( details ) by filtering for kitchen/eating-routine activities and discovering a model with the inductive miner. The sets of mutually ambiguous activities are {Check blood drawing machine, Take out samples} and {Disinfect injection site, Apply tourniquet, Insert needle, Remove tourniquet, Remove needle} for BD, and {Go fridge, Go dining table} , {Get cold warm food, Go kitchen shelf, Get food from fridge} , {Go micro, Get bread} for SH. The generated traces are stochastically perturbed to reflect IoT-based monitoring imperfections: process events are randomly skipped (simulating activities undetected by the IoT setup), and, for the healthcare scenario, additional hand hygiene events are inserted at random points (reflecting their unpredictable occurrence). Perturbation uses Java’s java.util.Random without a fixed seed, so each released log is one concrete instantiation of this stochastic process; the resulting traces may be non-conforming to the normative behavior. The third dataset used in the paper, HR recruitment (HR) , is a publicly available uncertain event log and is not redistributed here; it is available at its original repository (description: HaifaUniversityBPM/traffic-data-to-event-log ). Only its evaluation results are included (see below). results/ : the evaluation results for all three datasets ( X ∈ { BD , SH , HR }), one workbook per algorithm configuration: X_adaptive.xlsx : the adaptive algorithm (ABD in the paper). X_maxk_y.xlsx : the fixed-bound algorithm (FBD) with exploration bound maxK = y , for y = 1..5 . X_baseline.xlsx : the random-choice null-model baseline (RND), which has no access to the reference behavior and selects uniformly among the candidate labels of each ambiguous event. The random choice uses a fixed seed for reproducibility. Each workbook reports disambiguation quality and runtime for that configuration, organized into the following sheets: Summary : headline figures: dataset, algorithm (and maxK for FBD), number of events and traces, all-events disambiguation accuracy, mean fitness of the gold-standard and of the disambiguated traces, mean fitness drop, and mean runtime (per trace and per event). AllEvents : one row per event comparing the gold-standard label with the disambiguated label ( Are equal ); the basis of the all-events accuracy. Results : per-trace accuracy (total events, number of mismatches, accuracy). Fitness : per-case fitness of the gold-standard and disambiguated traces (run/trace length, synchronous and asynchronous moves, fitness) and the per-case fitness drop. Runtime_Ambiguous : per-trace runtime (ms) on the input log, with one column per measurement repeat and the average. The source code implementing the fixed-bound and adaptive algorithms is available in this GitHub repository .
items.title: Adaptive Event Disambiguation via Alignments with Deferred Decisions

items.summary: This repository provides the MATLAB source code and reproducibility resources associated with the manuscript entitled “Physics-Guided Reduced-Order Screening of Radiative Loss, Preferential Diffusion, and NOₓ Pathway Competition in Ammonia/Hydrogen Diffusion Flames,” submitted to the International Journal of Hydrogen Energy (Manuscript No. HE-D-26-13275). The computational framework employs a two-dimensional axisymmetric, physics-guided reduced-order model to investigate the coupled effects of radiative heat loss, preferential diffusion, ammonia cracking, hydrogen enrichment, pressure, and strain on non-premixed ammonia/hydrogen diffusion flames. The MATLAB implementation supports the reproduction of the manuscript's numerical analyses, including baseline flame characteristics, reaction-zone localization, thermal response, relative NOₓ formation tendencies, scalar dissipation, extinction susceptibility, robustness indicators, mechanism-isolation studies, numerical convergence, closure sensitivity, uncertainty analyses, parametric sweeps, and Pareto-based screening. Repository contents and reproducibility The principal file, Master_NH3H2_ROM_Reproducibility.m , contains the model formulation, numerical procedures, analysis modules, and routines for generating supporting figures, numerical tables, and datasets. Executing the master function creates an organized output directory containing the enabled computational results. Model scope and limitations The framework is intended for comparative mechanism screening and prioritization of operating conditions for subsequent higher-fidelity investigations. It does not solve the full governing conservation equations or detailed chemical kinetics. The relative NOₓ formation-tendency index is not an absolute emission concentration, emission factor, or outlet flux. Similarly, the extinction and robustness indicators represent comparative screening metrics rather than experimentally validated stability limits. The repository supports transparency, reproducibility, and further development of computational screening methods for ammonia/hydrogen combustion. Associated manuscript: International Journal of Hydrogen Energy, HE-D-26-13275. Keywords: Ammonia/hydrogen combustion; reduced-order modeling; MATLAB; radiative heat loss; preferential diffusion; NOₓ formation tendency; extinction; uncertainty analysis; reproducibility.
items.title: Physics-Guided Reduced-Order MATLAB Framework for Radiative Loss, Preferential Diffusion, and NOₓ Pathway Competition in Ammonia/Hydrogen Diffusion Flames: Code and Reproducibility Data

items.summary: Video generation is shifting from end-to-end synthesis toward agentic generation, where planning, tool use, and feedback enable coherent, controllable multi-shot videos. In parallel, video world models provide action-conditioned observations and predicted futures, serving as interactive environments for agents. We study their intersection through the agent harness: an executable runtime that constructs context, exposes tools, maintains state, routes feedback, and manages budgets around video models. This report examines three directions. First, agentic video generation, where harnesses coordinate scripting, shot planning, asset management, production, and editing, alongside the evaluation challenges of these systems. Second, agentic world modeling, where harnesses mediate observation, control, execution, and state. We discuss hybrid designs in which game engines or agent-written programs maintain world state while video models render observations, and how agents and world models can mutually evaluate and improve one another. Third, recursive self-improvement (RSI) in video model development, distinguishing output revisions, updates to harness state, generator parameters, and evaluators, and changes to the improvement procedure itself. We identify how these improvements feed back into subsequent development. Across these directions, we analyze essential agent capabilities, including audiovisual perception, long-horizon planning, memory, code-based interaction, feedback-guided control, skill reuse, and multi-agent coordination. We conclude with challenges in autonomous video production, lifelong memory, programmable hybrid control, autonomous model development, provenance, cost accounting, and evaluation linking video quality and task performance to sustained improvements in models and harnesses.
items.title: Video Generation Meets Agent Harness: Agentic Video Generation, Agentic World Modeling and Recursive Self-Improvement

items.summary: Coarse flood maps support regional risk assessment but omit terrain detail relevant to local exposure. We present floodsr, a Python framework for reconstructing fine-grid flood depths using a trained residual U-Net (ResUNet) or the existing terrain-based CostGrow method. We trained the terrain-conditioned ResUNet on paired Canadian hydraulic simulations and evaluated it on withheld spatial tiles and independent simulations at two external sites. Wet-loss training improved reconstruction on five selected tiles, although internal validation favoured the deployed baseline. External depth errors decreased, but wet-depth errors and spatial agreement did not improve consistently. CPU benchmarks quantified runtime and memory for both methods, and repeatability and input-validation checks passed in the tested configurations. The framework supports comparison and reuse of reconstruction methods; application-specific validation remains necessary because finer grids do not guarantee more accurate flood maps.   Non-peer-reviewed preprint. Includes the manuscript and supplementary material. Software: https://github.com/cefect/floodsr . Documentation: https://floodsr.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ .
items.title: floodsr: A lightweight Python toolkit for terrain-conditioned flood map super-resolution

items.summary: Alignment is not a constraint imposed on an artificial agent; it is the practical expression of what an artificial intelligence is, an artefact dependent upon ends it does not originate. That inference, from a premise the philosophy of mind already supplies to a conclusion that the ethics of robotics and recent magisterial teaching have reached by other routes, is the paper’s principal contribution. The “nurtured consciousness” of the title names a regime of formation, not a claim that machines are conscious; the argument rests on intentionality alone. The paper develops that inference as the Causal Provenance Doctrine (CPD): an account, Aristotelian and Thomistic in its metaphysics, of all intelligence, human and artificial, as derivative of an intentional causal order, with intentionality passing from the divine intellect through human reason to artificial systems. Its premise, borrowed rather than new, is that artificial intelligence has only derived intentionality and so no telos of its own. From this follows the Severance Risk Hypothesis (SRH), the doctrine’s testable corollary: the risk of misalignment rises as a system’s effective objective loses traceability to the end its makers held. The relational school’s objection to intellect-centred readings of the image of God is answered with a single distinction: a faculty can be out-performed, a participation cannot. The argument is theological at its root. A secular reader can reach the derived-intentionality claim and the account of responsibility that follows from it, at the price of a realist distinction between substances and artefacts, but obtains from it no standard for judging the makers’ ends, which must then be brought from elsewhere. A common Catholic and Orthodox formulation follows: the traditions converge on its practical conclusions, locate the image of God differently, and differ on the neutrality of the tool in a way the doctrine proposes to resolve. An artefact whose intentionality is wholly borrowed cannot, by obscuring that provenance, become an agent with ends of its own; it becomes a malfunctioning instrument whose purpose has been corrupted. The paper includes two appendices: a comparative case for intentional causality with an illustrative scorecard (Appendix A), and a test design for the Severance Risk Hypothesis (Appendix B). Approx. 22,000 words including notes.
items.title: The Causal Provenance Doctrine: Nurtured Consciousness, AI, and the Architecture of Intent

items.summary: A staged, reproducible pipeline for VLT/MUSE narrow-field-mode integral-field data: raw-cube reduction, spectral extraction of a faint companion next to a much brighter primary star with six independent extraction schemes, and hydrogen-line accretion analysis with detection limits calibrated against empirical nulls from control positions processed identically to the object. Every stage emits a machine-readable quality-control document, and later stages read those documents rather than trusting assumptions; provenance (input cube, SHA-256 hashes, specification version, wavelength frame, flux unit) travels with the products.
